# Results Table Template

Generated by `scripts/make_results.py` from MLflow. **Never hand-edited.**

---

## Caption rules (mandatory)

Every table in this project carries a caption that answers all five:

1. **Which split?** (`test_public` / `TEST_priv` / fixture)
2. **Which threshold, and where did it come from?** (`OP-FPR1` validation-derived / `OP-3SIGMA` /
   `OP-F1MAX` oracle)
3. **How many seeds**, and is the spread mean ± std?
4. **Whose implementation?** (`[OWN]` / `[LIB]`)
5. **Is anything test-selected or oracle?** — marked inline, never only in a footnote

A table without these is not reportable. Most published confusion in this field comes from tables
that silently mix integration limits, splits, or oracle thresholds.

The `DR-1 verdict` column is what makes this an experiment log rather than a collection of numbers.
Fill it at the time of the run, not retrospectively.

> Threshold frozen at the clean `OP-FPR1`. Realized FPR in parentheses.

The final column is the control. If the synthetic columns do not rank the models the same way it
does, say so plainly — that finding is worth more than the table it sits in.

## Pareto figure spec

`reports/figures/pareto.png` — accuracy vs cost, the figure a reader remembers.

- x: p95 latency (ms, log scale) · y: AU-PRO@0.05 · marker area: memory-bank size (MB)
- colour: tier · annotate the Pareto frontier · mark the 4 GB VRAM feasibility boundary
- one panel per category, plus a mean panel

## Negative results

`reports/negative-results.md`, one entry per abandoned line:

```
### <technique>
Hypothesis: <what you expected and why>
Configurations tried: <list, with config hashes>
Result: <numbers>
DR-1 verdict: rejected (<which clause failed>)
Interpretation: <why you think it failed>
Cost: <GPU-hours>
```

This file is a deliverable, not an apology. It is also the part of the report that most clearly
distinguishes measured work from demonstrated work.
